result.title: PEAR: Adaptive Advantage Reshaping for Perception and Exploration in Large Vision-Language Models
result.summary: Effective multimodal reasoning requires a model to reliably utilize visual information while sufficiently exploring diverse reasoning paths. To achieve this goal, prior work combines visual dependency and token entropy to reshape sequence-level advantages, but scaling the contribution of token entropy by visual dependency can leave high-entropy tokens with low visual dependency underweighted, despite their important role in reasoning exploration. To address this limitation, we propose PEAR, an adaptive advantage reshaping method for improving perception and exploration in multimodal reasoning. PEAR retains visual dependency as the base signal and adds an entropy-based exploration gain only at high-entropy positions, with lower visual dependency leading to a larger additional gain. The fused signal is then mapped to positive token-level weights that reshape the sequence-level advantage. Experiments on Qwen2.5-VL-3B/7B show that PEAR achieves the highest average performance among evaluated baselines across multimodal reasoning benchmarks, alongside leading results on textual reasoning and general multimodal benchmarks.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 PEAR，一种面向多模态推理的强化学习优势重整形方法：以视觉依赖度为基信号，在高熵位置额外加入与视觉依赖度负相关的探索增益，并映射为 token 级正权重来调整序列级优势。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接涉及 VLM 推理训练中视觉信息使用与探索的权衡，涉及视觉旁路、贡献分配和高熵 token 的探索价值，可供核查其与 latent 推理训练及视觉证据筛选的联系。
